actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

facts.text: The README presents the repository as a controller-design study that controls a whip, described as a complex object with significant dynamics
The README's setup downloads the requirements with pip for the mujoco-py simulation
The module defines class Simulation, documented as running a single whip simulation
The Simulation constructor loads the selected model with mjPy.load_model_from_path from C.MODEL_DIR + model_name + '.xml' and wraps it in mjPy.MjSim
Simulation reads n_act from the model's actuator_names, nq from its joint_names and dt from model.opt.timestep
Simulation.set_init_posture writes the caller's qpos and qvel into mj_data and calls mj_sim.forward; it takes no seed
Simulation.reset calls mj_sim.reset and resets each attached controller
Simulation.run halts the loop as unstable when max(abs(mj_data.qacc)) exceeds 10 ** 6
Simulation.get_state returns the concatenated mj_data.qpos and mj_data.qvel arrays
Simulation.stepML writes the action into mj_data.ctrl[:n_act] and calls mj_sim.step
The user-facing main_whip.py builds the model name as '3D_model_w_whip_T' + str(target_type)
The model root is '<mujoco model="1_3D_model_w_N25">' and its compiler declares the angle unit as radian
The option element sets timestep 0.0001 s, 50 iterations, the PGS solver, the Euler integrator and gravity 0 0 -9.81
The arm has four hinge joints named joint_shoulder_flex_ext, joint_shoulder_add_abd, joint_shoulder_med_lat and joint_elbow
The whip chain runs from body_whip_node1 to body_whip_node25, and every node carries an X hinge and a Y hinge
The target sphere geom has position 1.9950 0.0000 0.0000, size 0.03 and mass 0
The actuator section declares four motor actuators, one per arm joint, and each sets forcelimited false and states no ctrlrange

determinism.notes: The stand-in has no seed input and restores all-zero model defaults; it applies a deterministic placeholder velocity from each control value, which is not the engine's physics.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it parses the MJCF for the 54 hinge joints, the four motor actuators, their absent ctrlranges and the 0.0001 s option timestep, then moves each actuated hinge by a placeholder velocity proportional to its control value; it computes no inertia, gear, torque, gravity, contact, friction, constraint, damping or actuator dynamics and produces no MuJoCo trajectory
the stand-in loads no mesh or texture and resolves no collision, contact or sensor; the model's target sphere and whip inertias are not simulated

the fake reports no ctrlrange for the four motors, exactly as the model states; the bridge therefore publishes action.ctrl operator_required and site-limits.example.json is operator example data, not a model bound; a step that sets action.ctrl is refused until an operator overlay bounds it
the fake has no mj_getState, mj_setState, mj_stateSize or mjtState, so the bridge uses its basic checkpoint profile: time, qpos, qvel and ctrl are restored, not MuJoCo's full integration state

the upstream Simulation task interface is NOT COVERED: it applies the caller's qpos and qvel, makes the whip downwards, runs joint-impedance controllers and an objective, and uses a 10 ** 6 acceleration instability halt; the bridge serves raw ctrl and the integration state instead
the fake reset restores all-zero model defaults, not the initial posture that main_whip.py writes; cap.world.reset.v1 accepts a seed but does not use it
only models/3D_model_w_whip_T1.xml is served; the card's 2D_model_w_whip.xml and the N10-N20 and T2-T6 scenes are not
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so the stand-in was not compared with the real engine and the sim backend that imports mujoco was not run; no physical arm or whip is modelled

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.
measures.name: native_checkpoint

operator_required.name: step
operator_required.reason: the model gives none of its actuators no control range (ctrllimited false or no ctrlrange), so MuJoCo leaves the control unclamped; site-limits.json must bound action.ctrl before a step can set it

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state, including the last controls, is kept and stays readable. A later explicit step without action reuses those controls
